title: Until Dawn: Rush of Blood
subtitle: A haunted ride that keeps moving
summary: Until Dawn: Rush of Blood is Supermassive Games' virtual-reality rail shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016.
body: Until Dawn: Rush of Blood is Supermassive Games' virtual-reality rail shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016. A roller-coaster carriage carries the player through a horror-themed carnival, with enemies and targets appearing along the route. The ride controls the journey while the player aims and reacts to the threats around it. The premise makes the headset's enclosed viewpoint part of the attraction: the track continues forward, and the next disturbing scene can emerge beside the carriage as readily as ahead.

Seven roller-coaster stages combine moving scenery with shooting encounters. The player begins with handguns and finds other weapons along the way. Each section arranges targets and live enemies around the changing position of the cart, making looking and aiming inseparable from the ride's progress. A bend or sudden descent changes the angle of the next encounter without asking the player to steer. The game's limited route gives it control over timing, while the surrounding virtual space leaves the player responsible for noticing where danger has appeared.

The game draws locations and figures from Until Dawn into a more theatrical carnival structure. Hallucinations and shifting tracks let the familiar horror material transform as the ride progresses, connecting the separate shooting galleries through an increasingly unstable journey. Jason Graves composed the music. Released alongside the first PlayStation VR headset, Rush of Blood uses a recognizable amusement-park form to introduce its movement: the player is seated in a carriage, but the view around that seat supplies the scale and immediacy of the attraction.
